![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Piping `Get-VHD` directly to `Get-Disk` will fail because `Get-Disk` does not accept pipeline input of type `VirtualHardDisk`, nor does it automatically bind `DiskNumber` to the `-Number` parameter. To resolve this, explicitly query the updated VHD object after mounting and pass its `DiskNumber` to `Get-Disk -Number`.

```
    $vhd = Get-VHD -Path $poolPath
    if (-not $vhd.Attached) {
        Mount-VHD -Path $poolPath
    }
    $vhd = Get-VHD -Path $poolPath
    $disk = Get-Disk -Number $vhd.DiskNumber
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Using `exit 1` inside a script executed in an interactive PowerShell session will terminate the entire PowerShell host process, closing the user's terminal window. To align with the fail-closed error handling pattern used in the other scripts in this deployment bundle, use `throw` to signal validation failure instead of exiting the process.

```
if ($errors.Count -gt 0) {
    throw "Preflight validation failed with $($errors.Count) error(s)."
}
```
Fixed in eb63f28ad7dbbca038b302ad2a9a5041fba30201: re-read the VHD after Mount-VHD and resolve the disk explicitly with Get-Disk -Number $vhd.DiskNumber.
Fixed in eb63f28ad7dbbca038b302ad2a9a5041fba30201: preflight failures now throw after writing the result, preserving failure semantics without terminating an interactive PowerShell host.

When an operator passes `-DestroyPool` without `-AcknowledgePermanentDataLoss`, the script enters this block and can dismount the configured pool before the missing acknowledgement is checked later. That means a refused destructive request still mutates the host by taking runner storage offline, contradicting the rollback contract that every mutation needs an explicit acknowledgement.
